name: Wise
summary: Wise describes three steps on its jobs site: apply, interview and offer. The interview stage starts with a recruiter call of about 30 minutes on your experience, motivation and what you know about Wise. Engineers then have pair programming, system design, and a product and culture round; product managers have four to five interviews of about an hour, including product, stakeholder and leadership interviews. Wise says interviews are competency-based, recommends the STAR method, and says AI tools shouldn't be used in live coding or design rounds.
rounds: Recruiter call, about 30 minutes: your experience, motivation and what you know about Wise
Pair programming interview (engineering) or a role interview with the team
System design interview (engineering) or a stakeholder collaboration interview (product)
Final interview with leads, then an offer
looks_for: Customer focus: making money move cheaply, fast and simply

questions.text: Tell me about a time you took ownership of a problem nobody else was handling.
covers: The problem and why it was falling through the gaps
What you did
The result and what changed after

questions.text: Tell me about a time you made something simpler for customers.
covers: What was hard for them
What you changed
How you knew it helped

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to work with a team whose priorities differed from yours.
covers: What each side needed
How you found common ground
What you achieved

questions.text: Tell me about feedback you disagreed with at first.
covers: The feedback
How you thought it through
What you did and learned

questions.text: How would you design a service that shows customers a live exchange rate and fee before they send money?
covers: Rate sources and refresh frequency
Locking a quote for a short time
Showing fees clearly and handling rate changes

questions.text: How would you make an international transfer arrive faster for customers?
covers: Where time goes today: checks, banking networks, cut-offs
Options: local accounts, better routing, earlier checks
Measuring speed and keeping it safe

questions.text: Let's pair: write a function that converts an amount between currencies given a table of rates, then improve it together.
covers: Clarifying inputs, rounding and missing rates
Writing it step by step and talking through it
Tests and edge cases

questions.text: How would you decide which new country or currency to launch next?
covers: Customer demand and transfer corridors
Regulation and partner banks
A small launch to learn fast

questions.text: A customer's money is stuck mid-transfer. How would you investigate?
covers: Checking each step the transfer went through
Talking to the partner bank if needed
Keeping the customer updated

questions.text: What do you know about how Wise works and makes money?
covers: Wise's mission in your own words
How fees are shown and why that matters
Something you noticed using the product

questions.text: Why do you want to work at Wise?
covers: What draws you to Wise's mission
How your skills fit the role
What you'd like to improve for customers

questions.text: What questions do you have about the team or the product?
covers: How the team decides what to build
What success looks like
Something specific about Wise

tips: Read Wise's values and mission before the recruiter call; Wise says it expects you to know what it does.
Use the STAR method: Wise says its interviews are competency-based.
Don't use AI tools in live coding or design rounds; Wise says they shouldn't be used there.
Try sending a small transfer with Wise so you can talk about the product from experience.
